title: A limit, and the count it does not change
request:
the four keys under `n/`, but at most two of them

POST /v3/kv/range
{
  "key": "bi8=",
  "limit": "2",
  "range_end": "bjA="
}
note: count answers the question that was asked — how many keys are in this range — and limit only says how many of them to send. A server that reports the truncated length as the count makes paging impossible.

title: The last two keys, by sorting before truncating
request:
at most two keys under `n/`, largest first

POST /v3/kv/range
{
  "key": "bi8=",
  "limit": "2",
  "range_end": "bjA=",
  "sort_order": "DESCEND",
  "sort_target": "KEY"
}
note: The sort happens first and the limit second. Truncating to the first two keys and then reversing them would answer `n/1` and `n/0`, which is a different pair of keys, not a different order.
